examples.ko: 여행 때 일어난 재미있는 에피소드를 들려줄게요.
examples.en: I'll tell you a funny episode that happened on my trip.
This drama has sixteen episodes.

examples.ko: 어제 본 에피소드가 너무 슬퍼서 울었어요.
examples.en: The episode I watched yesterday was so sad that I cried.
I watched everything from the first episode to the last.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 데뷔 에피소드는 아주 유명해요.
examples.en: The story of how that singer debuted is very famous.

examples.ko: 에피소드마다 이야기가 달라서 순서 없이 봐도 돼요.
examples.en: Each episode has a different story, so you can watch in any order.

explain: 드라마와 웹툰의 한 편은 '회'라고도 하는데, 에피소드는 그 한 편 또는 한 편 속 이야기에 써요. 사람 이야기에서는 '일화'보다 '에피소드'가 입말에서 더 자주 나와요. '에피소드가 있다'고 하면 남에게 들려줄 만한 재미있는 일이 있다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: I have lots of funny episodes from my trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남에게 들려줄 만한 재미있는 일을 말할 때 자주 짝지어 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for a fun story worth telling others.

phrases.en: There's a story behind this photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 일에 남에게 말해 줄 이야기가 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means there is a story about it worth sharing.

phrases.en: I watched the last episode of the drama yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드라마나 웹툰의 마지막 한 편을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the final installment of a drama or webtoon.

explain_en: One installment of a drama or webtoon can also be called '회', while 'episode' covers that installment or a story inside it. When telling stories about people, '에피소드' appears in speech more than the stiffer '일화'. '에피소드가 있다' hints at something fun worth retelling.

examples.en: A new singer is born today.
Do you know how this song came to be?
I took a photo of the moment it was born.
When a new government is born, policies change.
She is the first writer to come out of our class.
I think a good film will be born.

explain: '태어나다'는 사람과 동물에게 일상에서 써요. '탄생하다'는 새 나라, 작품, 스타처럼 큰 의미가 있을 때 써요. 대화에서 사람이 태어난 이야기는 '태어나다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I was born in Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 동물이 태어날 때 일상에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday word for people or animals being born.

phrases.example: 낡은 건물이 멋진 카페로 새롭게 탄생했어요.
phrases.en: The old building was reborn as a nice cafe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무언가 새로 만들어져 의미가 클 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when something new is made and it feels meaningful.

phrases.en: We celebrated the birth of the new baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '탄생'을 써서 태어난 일을 크게 기뻐할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun '탄생' is used when celebrating a birth in a big way.

explain_en: '태어나다' is the everyday word for people and animals. '탄생하다' fits significant beginnings like a new country, a work, or a star. For a person's birth in conversation, '태어나다' sounds natural.

dis.h: come into being; great person, new thing

p.n: 태어나다 is for living beings, so it sounds unnatural for a country coming into being.

t90.ax: A new singer is born today.

examples.en: The party primary is held next week.
He won the primary and became the candidate.
I am waiting for the primary results.
The two candidates competed fiercely in the primary.
I joined the party to take part in the primary.
The leader is chosen through a primary.

explain: '경선'은 후보를 정하는 선거이고, 그 뒤에 치르는 선거는 '본선'이라고 해요. '경선을 치르다', '경선에서 이기다'처럼 써요. 일반 투표를 말하는 '선거'와는 구별해서 써요.

phrases.en: The two candidates hold a primary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경선을 한다는 뜻으로 자주 같이 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation for holding a primary.

phrases.example: 그는 경선에서 져서 후보가 되지 못했어요.
phrases.en: He lost the primary and couldn't become the candidate.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경선에서 이기다'의 반대로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of winning in a primary.

phrases.en: After the primary ends, the main election begins.
phrases.nuance_ko: 후보를 정한 뒤에 치르는 선거로, '경선'과 짝이 되는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The election held after candidates are chosen; the counterpart of 경선.

explain_en: '경선' is the election to pick a candidate, and the election held afterward is the '본선'. Common phrases are '경선을 치르다' (hold a primary) and '경선에서 이기다' (win the primary). It is kept separate from '선거', the general word for an election.

examples.ko: 폭설 때문에 산골 마을이 이틀 동안 고립됐어요.
examples.en: The mountain village was cut off for two days because of heavy snow.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 무인도에 고립된 사람들 이야기예요.
examples.en: That movie is about people stranded on a deserted island.

examples.ko: 친구가 없어서 학교에서 혼자 고립되는 느낌이에요.
examples.en: I have no friends, so I feel isolated at school.
The bridge collapsed, and the village almost got cut off.
To avoid becoming isolated, talk with people often.

examples.ko: 길이 막혀서 차 안에 몇 시간 고립돼 있었어요.
examples.en: The road was blocked, so I was stuck in the car for hours.

explain: 마을이나 섬 같은 장소가 다른 곳과 끊길 때도, 사람이 주변과 관계가 끊길 때도 써요. '외롭다'는 마음의 느낌이고 '고립되다'는 놓인 상황이에요. 보통 피동형으로 쓰고, 일부러 그렇게 만들면 '고립시키다'예요.

phrases.example: 눈 때문에 고립된 마을에 구조대가 갔어요.
phrases.en: A rescue team went to the village cut off by snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 곳과 길이 끊긴 장소를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a place cut off from others.

phrases.en: He is isolated at work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주변과 관계가 끊긴 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a state of being cut off from people around you.

phrases.example: 친구들이 그 아이를 고립시키면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: Friends should not isolate that child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 다른 사람을 외톨이로 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when deliberately leaving someone alone.

explain_en: It works for places cut off from others, like villages and islands, and for people cut off from those around them. '외롭다' is a feeling, while '고립되다' describes the situation. It is usually used in the passive; doing it to someone on purpose is '고립시키다'.

t90.ax: I have no friends, so I feel isolated at school.

examples.ko: 그 가수가 갑자기 인기 스타로 급부상했어요.
examples.en: That singer suddenly rose to become a popular star.

examples.ko: 새로운 기술의 급부상이 시장을 바꾸고 있어요.
examples.en: The sudden rise of the new technology is changing the market.

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 우승 후보로 급부상하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is suddenly emerging as a title contender.

examples.ko: 이 동네는 맛집 거리로 급부상한 곳이에요.
examples.en: This neighborhood is a place that has suddenly become a famous food street.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 그 회사의 급부상을 크게 다뤘어요.
examples.en: The news covered that company's sudden rise at length.

examples.ko: 작년에 급부상한 배우가 올해는 영화에 나와요.
examples.en: The actor who suddenly rose to fame last year appears in a movie this year.

explain: 주로 '급부상하다'로 써요. 사람, 회사, 나라가 짧은 시간에 눈에 띄게 올라올 때 쓰고, 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 천천히 올라오면 '성장하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 그 식당이 요즘 인기 맛집으로 급부상했어요.
phrases.en: That restaurant has suddenly risen as a popular spot lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주로 이렇게 동사로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is mostly used as a verb like this.

phrases.en: The singer who rose suddenly appeared on TV.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 사람이나 단체를 붙여 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies a person or group that follows.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 경제 강국으로 급부상 중이에요.
phrases.en: That country is rapidly rising as an economic power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 빠르게 올라오고 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is rising fast right now.

explain_en: Mostly used as the verb 급부상하다. It is common in the news for a person, company or country that stands out in a short time. For slower growth, 성장하다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: The police sealed off the accident scene.
It snowed a lot, so they close off the mountain road.
The government may seal the border.
They sealed off the entrance and evacuated people.

examples.ko: 도로를 봉쇄하는 바람에 차가 못 지나갔어요.
examples.en: Because the road was blocked off, cars could not pass.

examples.ko: 병원이 건물을 봉쇄해서 아무도 못 들어가요.
examples.en: The hospital sealed the building, so no one can enter.

explain: 봉쇄하다는 길, 문, 국경을 막아서 드나들지 못하게 할 때 써요. 뉴스에서 '도로 봉쇄', '국경 봉쇄'처럼 자주 보여요. 그냥 문을 닫는 건 '닫다', 길을 막는 건 '막다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The police blocked the road because of the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 막아 차가 못 다니게 할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for closing a road to traffic.

phrases.en: The mountain road was blocked because of snow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길이 막혀서 드나들 수 없게 된 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a road that has been closed off.

phrases.en: There was news about a border closure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 보이는 명사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase often seen in the news.

explain_en: 봉쇄하다 is for blocking roads, doors or borders so nobody can get in or out. News often shows '도로 봉쇄' and '국경 봉쇄'. Simply closing a door is '닫다' and blocking a road is '막다'.

t90.ax: The government may seal the border.

examples.en: The enemy's surprise attack began at night.
Everyone was shocked by the sudden attack.

examples.ko: 곰의 습격을 받은 마을 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard a story about a village hit by a bear attack.

examples.ko: 경찰은 은행 습격 사건을 조사하고 있어요.
examples.en: The police are investigating the bank raid.
The attack was over within a few minutes.
This movie starts with an alien attack.

explain: '습격을 받다', '습격을 당하다', '습격을 막다'처럼 써요. 사람, 동물, 군대가 갑자기 공격할 때 쓰고, 미리 알린 싸움에는 쓰지 않아요. 뉴스와 영화에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: I was attacked by thieves during the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 공격을 받아 피해를 입었다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It strongly suggests being suddenly attacked and suffering harm.

phrases.en: The soldiers stopped the enemy's attack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑작스러운 공격을 지켜 내는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when defending against a sudden attack.

phrases.en: There was a store raid incident yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 갑작스러운 공격 사고를 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common news collocation for incidents of sudden attacks.

explain_en: Say '습격을 받다', '습격을 당하다' or '습격을 막다'. It fits sudden attacks by people, animals or armies, not a fight announced in advance. You hear it often in news and movies.

examples.en: That drama created a craze nationwide.
The idol craze spread overseas.
The news introduced a new craze.
My grandmother didn't know what a syndrome was.

examples.ko: 피로 신드롬을 앓는 직장인이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The number of office workers suffering from fatigue syndrome is growing.

examples.ko: 한동안 그 노래는 거의 신드롬 수준이었어요.
examples.en: For a while, that song was almost at craze level.

explain: 의학에서는 여러 증상이 함께 나타나는 상태를 '증후군'이라고 하고, 일상에서는 사회적으로 크게 유행하는 현상을 '신드롬'이라고 해요. 그래서 '○○ 신드롬을 일으키다'가 많이 쓰여요. 비슷한 '열풍'은 뜨거운 인기를 강조해요.

phrases.en: That movie became a phenomenon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것이 사회적으로 크게 유행하는 현상이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something grows into a big social craze.

phrases.example: 새 게임이 전 세계에 신드롬을 일으켰어요.
phrases.en: The new game set off a craze around the world.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신드롬'과 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 말로, 큰 유행을 만들었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common partner of 신드롬, meaning something created a big trend.

phrases.example: 요즘 건강 음식 열풍이 불고 있어요.
phrases.en: These days there is a craze for healthy food.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신드롬'과 비슷하지만 뜨거운 인기가 퍼지는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 신드롬 but with a stronger sense of hot popularity spreading.

explain_en: In medicine the Korean term is 증후군, while in daily life 신드롬 means a phenomenon that sweeps through society. A typical use is ○○ 신드롬을 일으키다. 열풍 is similar but stresses the heat of popularity.

en: to cause; to bring about; to lead to

examples.ko: 이 문제는 큰 혼란을 야기할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This problem could cause great confusion.
A small mistake led to an accident.
Excessive dieting brings about health problems.
That remark caused controversy, so he apologized.

examples.ko: 소음이 이웃 간의 갈등을 야기하기도 해요.
examples.en: Noise can sometimes cause conflict between neighbors.

examples.ko: 오해를 야기하지 않도록 정확하게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please speak precisely so as not to cause misunderstanding.

explain: 주로 문제, 갈등, 혼란, 논란처럼 좋지 않은 결과를 일으킬 때 써요. 일상에서는 '일으키다'를 쓰고, '야기하다'는 글이나 뉴스, 발표에서 많이 나와요. 소리가 비슷한 '이야기'와는 다른 말이에요.

phrases.example: 게임을 너무 오래 하면 건강 문제를 야기할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Playing games too long can cause health problems.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋지 않은 결과와 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with bad results.

phrases.en: That advertisement caused controversy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in the news.

phrases.en: That remark caused a misunderstanding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '야기하다' 대신 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday word used instead of '야기하다'.

explain_en: It is mostly used for causing unwelcome results such as problems, conflict, confusion and controversy. In daily talk people say '일으키다', while '야기하다' appears in writing, news and presentations. It is a different word from '이야기' (story), though they sound alike.

en: to be taken over; to be acquired (a company, business, or duty)

examples.en: That company was acquired by a large corporation.
The small shop changed its name when it was taken over.
Even after the takeover, the staff work as before.
I want to stop it from being acquired by a rival.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 작년에 다른 회사에 인수돼서 서비스가 달라졌어요.
examples.en: This app was acquired by another company last year, and its service changed.
Before it was acquired, it was running at a loss.

explain: '인수하다'는 사는 쪽, '인수되다'는 넘어가는 회사가 주어예요. 보통 '~에/에게 인수되다'로 써요. 뉴스에서 '대기업에 인수됐다'처럼 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: That restaurant was taken over by a new owner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 넘겨받을 때는 '에게'를, 회사나 기관이 넘겨받을 때는 '에'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '에게' for a person taking over, and '에' for a company or organization.
phrases.en_equiv: to be taken over by a new owner

phrases.en: That company has not been taken over yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 넘어가지 않았다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning the takeover has not happened.

phrases.example: 회사가 인수된 뒤에 직원들이 많이 바뀌었어요.
phrases.en: After the company was taken over, many employees changed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인수된 뒤에'로 넘어간 다음에 생긴 일을 이어서 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '인수된 뒤에' links what happened after the takeover.

explain_en: With '인수하다' the buyer is the subject; with '인수되다' the company being taken over is. It usually appears as '~에/에게 인수되다'. In the news you may hear '대기업에 인수됐다'.

examples.en: When the rain stopped, the suspended game was resumed.
Bus service will resume next week.
When will the stalled negotiations resume?

examples.ko: 점검이 끝나서 서비스가 곧 재개될 거예요.
examples.en: The check is done, so the service will resume soon.

examples.ko: 공사가 재개되면 소음이 다시 심해질 것 같아요.
examples.en: If the construction resumes, the noise will probably get bad again.

examples.ko: 오래 막혔던 대화가 아직도 재개되지 않았어요.
examples.en: The long-blocked talks still haven't resumed.

explain: 멈췄던 일이 다시 이어질 때만 써요. 처음 시작하는 일에는 쓰지 않아요. 공사, 협상, 운행, 경기 같은 말과 자주 나오고, 하는 사람이 있으면 '재개하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Construction resumed after winter passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 멈췄던 공사가 다시 이어질 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when stopped construction continues again.

phrases.en: The shop will resume business next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하는 사람이 있을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when there is a person or party doing the resuming.

phrases.en: Classes start again from tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 쉬운 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler everyday expression.

explain_en: It is only used when something that stopped starts again, never for a first start. It often goes with construction, negotiations, service and games. When someone does it on purpose, use the active form '재개하다'.

examples.en: The people rebuilt the collapsed bridge.
The government plans to rebuild the city.

examples.ko: 마을을 재건하는 데 오 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took five years to rebuild the village.
Everyone worked hard to rebuild the company.

examples.ko: 불에 탄 절을 재건해서 다시 열었어요.
examples.en: They rebuilt the temple that burned down and reopened it.

examples.ko: 폐허 위에 마을을 재건하고 학교도 세웠어요.
examples.en: They rebuilt the village on the ruins and put up a school too.

explain: 무너지거나 없어진 큰 것을 새로 세울 때 써요. 건물뿐 아니라 회사, 나라, 삶에도 써요. 작은 물건은 '고치다'를 쓰고, 부서진 것을 원래대로 되돌리는 일은 '복구하다'를 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The villagers are rebuilding their houses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다시 세우는 일이 지금도 진행 중일 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A conjugated form used when the rebuilding is still in progress.

phrases.en: People rebuilt the country after the war.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물만이 아니라 나라 전체를 다시 세운다는 큰 뜻으로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the word can be used in a large sense, rebuilding a whole country rather than just buildings.

phrases.en: I built the collapsed house again.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재건하다'와 비슷한 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to '재건하다' and easier to use in everyday conversation.

explain_en: Use it for raising something big that collapsed or disappeared. It works for buildings and also for companies, countries and lives. Small items are just '고치다', and restoring something broken to its original state is more often '복구하다'.

t90.ax: The people rebuilt the collapsed bridge.

examples.en: A big tragedy was reported on the news.
Many people were hurt in that tragedy.
The government is investigating the cause of the disaster.

examples.ko: 다시는 이런 참사가 일어나지 않아야 해요.
examples.en: A tragedy like this must never happen again.
People laid flowers at the site of the tragedy.

examples.ko: 그 참사를 잊지 않으려고 기념식을 열어요.
examples.en: They hold a memorial ceremony so that the tragedy is not forgotten.

explain: 참사는 사고나 사건으로 사람이 많이 죽거나 다친 끔찍한 일을 말해요. 뉴스에서는 '대형 참사', '참사 현장'처럼 나오고, 가벼운 사고에는 쓰지 않아요. '일어나다', '막다'와 함께 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그 대형 참사는 오래 잊히지 않았어요.
phrases.en: That major tragedy was not forgotten for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피해가 아주 큰 사고를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an accident with very large damage.

phrases.example: 안전 점검으로 참사를 막을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Safety checks can prevent a disaster.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 사고를 예방한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to prevent a big accident.

phrases.en: A terrible tragedy happened there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사건이 생겼다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that an event occurred.

explain_en: 참사 refers to a terrible event in which many people are killed or hurt. In the news it appears as '대형 참사' and '참사 현장'. It is not used for minor accidents, and it often goes with '일어나다' and '막다'.

t90.ax: Many people were hurt in that tragedy.

en: to be propelled; to be pushed; to be driven

examples.en: The new plan will be pushed forward from next month.

examples.ko: 공원 만드는 일이 빠르게 추진되고 있어요.
examples.en: The park project is moving ahead quickly.
That project was driven by the city.
The plan went ahead as scheduled.
The work couldn't move forward for lack of money.
It is scheduled to go ahead within this year.

explain: '추진되다'는 계획이나 사업이 실제로 진행될 때 써요. '계획이 추진되다', '사업이 추진되다'처럼 계획이나 정책이 주어예요. 뉴스와 공문에서 많이 보여요. 사람이 하면 '계획을 추진하다'예요.

phrases.en: The new road is scheduled to go ahead next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로의 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about future plans.

phrases.en: The project is moving ahead smoothly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 문제없이 진행될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things go forward without problems.

phrases.en: The plan couldn't go ahead because there was no budget.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하려던 일이 진행되지 않았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something planned did not move forward.

explain_en: 추진되다 is used when a plan or project actually goes forward. Plans and policies are the subject, as in '계획이 추진되다'. It shows up a lot in news and official documents. When a person does it, use '계획을 추진하다'.
